findings: Eye-tracked foveation: the sharp region followed the gaze more promptly than with 1.0.0.4 (eye cameras at 90 pictures a second, 50 to 57 gaze samples a second) but, by the maintainer's account, only near the middle of the view. Baballonia reports only the range of eye angles its calibration covered, at most 45 degrees, and nothing measured how far the gaze reached.
Colour: the 1.0.0.5 check measured black at 0 but white at 297 of 1023 (mid grey at 100) from AMF's P010 converter, as if mapped for HDR, so every stream fell back to 8-bit (blacks stayed black).

Network: the 1.0.0.5 test on the 1 Gbit/s USB Ethernet adapter lost nothing up to 300 Mbit/s but judged 150 Mbit/s late: the host's sender, a Python loop at about 50 microseconds per datagram, took about 9.5 ms to send each 150 Mbit/s frame. Automatic bitrate chose 50 Mbit/s.

Controllers: models held still against each other overlapped by about 10 mm on the stream but touched exactly on the headset's own PC (the maintainer's observation). The stream predicts poses about 40 to 45 ms ahead at full frame rate (ALVR's estimate), so a controller that stops suddenly also overshoots for a moment.

Timing: 74 to 75 new frames a second at 75 Hz for most of the session at 2560 per eye with eye-tracked foveation (1216 x 1216 per eye sent); ALVR's pipeline estimate 37 to 44 ms (median 43.7) over the 75 full-rate samples the report kept.
changes: patches/0020-host-colour-variants-and-gaze-reach.patch: the AMD colour conversion tries a plain-SDR converter first (BT.709 transfer and primaries, tone mapping copy, no HDR metadata, no linear RGB), then 1.0.0.5's settings, each checked with the test picture and logged (VROST_COLOR_PROBE; variant= on VROST_COLOR); the gaze and sharp-region extremes per 5-second window on VROST_GAZE_FOVEATION (gaze_yaw, gaze_pitch, region_x, region_y), whose current region centres are logged only while they do not follow the gaze; the still-controller distances as received and as submitted, with the largest move and turn the host applied (VROST_CONTROLLER_PAIR)
client/device/prediction_check.hpp, client/device/openvr_device.cpp: the controllers' prediction miss per hand (moving and held still) and the distance between still controllers in the INPUT line

launcher/gaze_provider.py, eye_tracking.py, app.py, desktop.html, game_ui.py: the gaze reach per session (1st and 99th percentiles in whole degrees) with Measure again, on the page, in Game Mode and in reports; calibration steps that turn the head far enough each way
launcher/link_test.py, network_test.py, app.py: a step is late only for the spread the network added (arrival spread less the sender's own); a 1.0.0.5 result limited by lateness is tested again
launcher/app.py, timeline.py, host/events.py: the controllers' prediction in reports and the timeline; the controller pair line read on the host

launcher/headset.py: the foveated size estimate rounds as ALVR does (f32 arithmetic), so the page no longer shows a size one 32-pixel step too large in four combinations (for example 1824 where the host sends 1792)
tests/test_desktop_ui.js: the page checks brought up to date (they had fallen behind the 1.0.0.3 eye view) and run from the Python suite

docs/TECHNICAL_REFERENCE.md with its PDF (scripts/render_reference.py): how it works end to end and where it differs from ALVR, ALVR's clients, a directly connected headset, SteamVR's defaults and Baballonia; README: minimum and recommended specs; stale patch counts, sizes and latency figures corrected in other documents
Version 1.0.0.6 on both programs; documents and release notes
review: Two independent fact-checks of the technical reference against the code, the patched ALVR source and the 1.0.0.5 reports returned 39 findings (wrong numbers, over-claims, imprecise statements), all corrected before these packages were built. Two led to code changes: the foveated size estimate (launcher/headset.py), and the driver's log, which wrote the gaze-placed region centres every 5 seconds although the documents said where you look is never logged (patch 0020 now writes them only for a fixed or optical centre).
